- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- When sentiment is strongly bearish (≤-0.33), model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–2% to account for mean reversion or short-term rebound.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days); apply a “cool-down” correction: subtract 0.5–1.5% from forecast 2–3 days post-spike.
- Forecast horizon 30d often exhibits lag: true price moves faster than model; adjust by adding 0.5–1.0% to forecast if sentiment is neutral or mildly bullish.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles (e.g., 0.33, 1.00, -0.33), model tends to misalign with sentiment direction; align forecast slope with sentiment trend direction.
- When true price drops sharply after forecast peak (e.g., >3% drop from forecast max), reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 3–5 days to avoid overconfidence in momentum.
